name: atis-api
description:
# **ATIS API Overview**

This document outlines the ATIS API, designed for developers to access and query ATIS Content managed by the ATIS Platform. The ATIS API is a RESTful interface that facilitates querying and accessing various ATIS content from their respective sanity datasets.

## **Access**
---
Consumers of this API will have already been issued an API key by Travel Alberta via their subscription email. If you have not received an API key, please reach out to [services@travelalberta.com](mailto:services@travelalberta.com).

## **API Key Security**
---
Please be reminded that it is your responsibility to keep your API key secure. To prevent unauthorized access and potential misuse, ensure that your key is stored in a safe and secure location.

If you suspect that your API key has been lost, compromised, or exposed, please contact our support team at [services@travelalberta.com](mailto:services@travelalberta.com) for further assistance and to report the issue.

## **Authentication**
---
The ATIS API uses the `x-api-header` header to authenticate requests. You will need to include Authorization: `x-api-header: <API Access Token>` in the header for all requests.

## **Rate Limit**
---
Rate limiting is applied on a per usage plan basis. The default usage plan for Travel Alberta consumers have the following limits:
- 20 requests per second.
- 40 requests burst (number of requests the ATIS API can handle concurrently).
- 10,000 request per day.

If you exceed any of the limits above, you will be unable to make further API requests and will receive a `429 Too many requests` error until the next time window begins.

## **API Format**
---
After subscribing, all call definitions require the hostname and environment. The URI format will be as follows: `https://<hostname>/{environment}/{endpoint}`. The hostname and environments can be found in the **Base Documentation** section of this document, and the specific `endpoints` are detailed in the Endpoints section of this document.

Every request to the ATIS API must include a `version` query parameter specifying a valid API version. To view the latest available version, please refer to the changelog below.

### **Example Request**
```javascript
const myHeaders = new Headers();
myHeaders.append("x-api-key", "YOUR_API_KEY");

const requestOptions = {
  method: "GET",
  headers: myHeaders,
  redirect: "follow"
};

fetch("https://atis-api.travelalberta.com/development/listings?version=1&limit=10&sort=desc&sortBy=name&page=1", requestOptions)
  .then((response) => response.text())
  .then((result) => console.log(result))
  .catch((error) => console.error(error));
```

## **CORS**
---
Currently, the ATIS API supports the Cross-Origin Resource Sharing (CORS) protocol in production. This means that web applications may not be able to access the production API via client-side fetch calls within a browser unless their domains are whitelisted with Travel Alberta. Any domain not currently whitelisted will throw an error 403 response.

To enable your web application to make cross-origin requests to our API, please reach out to Travel Alberta. Submit a list of domains associated with your web application, and we will whitelist them with our API.

## **Caching**
---
Application side caching is crucial for improving the speed and responsiveness of web applications by reducing server load and minimizing network latency. A common example of this is by utilizing the `Cache-Control` header.
- Cache-Control HTTP Headers: Servers can instruct the browser on how long to cache resources using headers like Cache-Control. For instance, setting Cache-Control: max-age=3600 tells the browser to cache the resource for 3600 seconds (1 hour).

## **Change Log**
---
All notable changes to this API will be documented in this section.

### **2026-02-25**
---
### **Changed**
- Switched Sanity queries from `GET` to `POST` to support larger queries and proper GROQ parameter handling.

### **2026-01-30**
---
### **Changed**
- `GET /listings/`: Added support to both Version 1 and Version 2 of the api for a `featured` query parameter that orders results based on a comma-separated list of ListingIds.
- The `GET /events/` endpoint is unchanged.

### **2025-12-12**
---
### **Changed**
- `GET /events/`: If there is category and types in the query string the result set contains both filters as OR. (category || types).
- The `GET /listings/` endpoint is unchanged.

### **2025-08-12**
---
### **Fixed**
- API limit increased to 1000 requests per request.

### **Added**
- Added amenities to the categories endpoint.
- Added regions endpoint to support a specific travelalberta.com feature.

### **2025-07-03**
---
### **Added**
- Added new categories to the product taxonomy.

### **Changed**
- Setting isCoverPhoto field to true for the first image.

### **2025-04-16**
---
### **Added**
- Introduced version 2, retrieved by setting the `version` query parameter to `2`.

### **Changed**
- [version 2]: The `GET /listings/:_id` endpoint now returns amenities and highlights as an array of objects consistent with the `GET /listings` endpoint.
- The `regions` filter parameter for the `GET /listings` endpoint is now case insensitive, enhancing query flexibility.

### **Added**
- Introduced the  `GET /listings-geojson` endpoint to support GeoJSON-driven development.

### **2025-03-12**
---
### **Added**
- Added amenities to the categories endpoint.
- Added regions endpoint to support a specific travelalberta.com feature.

### **[version 1] - 2024-07-01**
---
### **Added**
- Added support for retrieving category taxonomy data.
- Added support for retrieving paginated organizations data.
- Added support for retrieving a single organization by id.
- Added support for retrieving paginated listings data.
- Added support for retrieving a single listing by id.

### **Changed**
- Localization and market endpoints are obsolete, and no longer supported.
- Events are now listings with the `availability` parameter set to `temporary`.
- Querying listings by `activities` is now replaced by querying by `highlights`.



## **Base Documentation**
---
### **Transport Layer Security (TLS) 1.2 Support**
Our API supports and has TLS 1.2 enabled to ensure secure communication between clients and servers. TLS 1.2 provides enhanced security features, including stronger encryption algorithms and improved handshake protocols, which protect your data from interception and tampering during transmission.

For optimal security, we recommend that all API clients are configured to use TLS 1.2.

### **Content Encoding and Body Size Limit**

Our API supports content encoding to optimize data transfer. Content encoding reduces the size of the response body, enhancing performance and reducing bandwidth usage.
Please note that the maximum allowable size for the request body is 10 MB. Requests exceeding this limit will be rejected to ensure optimal performance and reliability.
